newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-MCGWIRE MONSTER HOMER HELPS A'S OVERCOME RANDY JOHNSON.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-MCGWIRE MONSTER HOMER HELPS A'S OVERCOME RANDY JOHNSON.

text.p: Mark McGwire launched the longest home run in the history of the Kingdome and Steve Karsay threw six scoreless innings as the Oakland Athletics overcame a 19-strikeout performance by Randy Johnson for a 4-1 victory over the Seattle Mariners on Tuesday.
Geronimo Berroa and McGwire delivered RBI doubles in the third inning to stake Oakland to a 2-0 lead.

In the fifth, McGwire crushed his 27th homer of the season well into the upper deck of the Kingdome -- 538-feet -- for the longest homer in the majors this season and the longest ever hit at Seattle's Kingdome.
Karsay (2-7) allowed just three hits and two walks with five strikeouts for the win.

Johnson (11-2), who saw his six-game winning streak snapped, struck out 18 over the first eight innings. After giving up a solo homer to George Williams in the ninth, he got Mark Bellhorn looking for his 19th whiff of the game -- one shy of Roger Clemens's major-league record.
He tied Steve Carlton's mark for a left-hander, set in 1969. But despite the 19 Ks and no walks, Johnson was far from his best, giving up 11 hits and four runs.
In Detroit, the New York Yankees managed to blow a six-run lead before pulling out a 12-9 victory over the Tigers, thanks to the heroics of Tino Martinez and Chad Curtis.
Martinez went 5-for-5 with four RBIs and his 24th and 25th home runs and Curtis homered and drove in five runs as the pair accounted for nine of New York's 12 runs.
The Yankees saw a 9-3 lead disappear on Damion Easley's two run homer in the bottom of the sixth and Melvin Nieves's three-run shot in a four-run seventh.

But Martinez belted his second homer of the game off Mike Myers (0-4) in the ninth to put the Yanks back in front and former Tiger Curtis added two insurance runs with a two-run homer off Doug Brocail for the final margin.

In Cleveland, Jim Thome had two hits, including his 11th homer this month, and Sandy Alomar added a two-run double to extend his hitting streak to 23 games as the Indians doubled up the Minnesota Twins 10-5.

Thome connected off Minnesota starter Dave Stevens (0-1) in the third inning for his third homer in the last two games and 21st of the season. Brian Giles and Matt Williams also homered for the Indians.
Jaret Wright (1-0) won in his major league debut, allowing five runs and seven hits in 5 2/3 innings. Stevens was tagged for six runs and seven hits in just three innings.

In Chicago, Wilson Alvarez and two relievers combined on a five-hitter and Ozzie Guillen and Harold Baines drove in two runs apiece as the White Sox blanked the Kansas City Royals 4-0 for their fourth straight win.
Alvarez (6-6) allowed four hits and two walks while striking out five in eight innings.
Guillen had a two-run single in the second and Baines had a two-run double in the third. Both hits came off starter Jim Pittsley (2-5), who allowed eight hits in seven innings.
In Toronto, Nomar Garciaparra and Darren Bragg homered and John Valentin's two-run double capped a five-run second inning as the Boston Red Sox beat the Blue Jays 9-6.

John Wasdin (2-3), the third Boston pitcher, picked up the win, allowing two hits in three scoreless innings. Luis Andujar (0-4) was roughed up for seven runs and nine hits with two walks in just 1 2/3 innings.
Garciaparra had four hits and scored four times with a solo homer in the fifth. Bragg's hit a two-run homer in the first and the Red Sox broke open a 2-2 game with five runs in the second.

In Milwaukee, Cal Ripken capped a five-run second inning with a two-run double and Arthur Rhodes delivered four outstanding innings of relief to lead the Baltimore Orioles to a 6-2 victory over the Brewers.
Roberto Alomar also had a two-run single in the second for the Orioles.

Rhodes was perfect in his first save of the season, throwing 27 of 41 pitches for strikes. Shawn Boskie (4-3), who allowing two runs and four hits in five-plus innings got the win. Milwaukee's Scott Karl (2-9) gave up six runs as his winless drought stretched to five starts.
At Texas, Craig Grebeck's double scored Luis Alicea in the ninth inning to lift the Anaheim Angels a 7-6 win over the Rangers in a meeting of teams headed in opposite directions.

With one out in the ninth, Alicea doubled to deep right off Xavier Hernandez (0-1). John Wetteland relieved and Grebeck grounded a 3-1 pitch down the left-field line to score Alicea as the Angels posted their sixth successive win while extending the Rangers' slide to seven.
Rich DeLucia (6-2) retired Ivan Rodriguez for the final out in the eighth inning to pick up the win.
